mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT continue rising from their current depressed levels, commuting and downtown foot traffic should keep recovering, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks relative to the last four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not exceed its last-4-week mean over the next 28 days while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both continue to trend upward week over week.

mechanism_narrative: A continued rise in RESIDENTIAL time indicates more time spent near home; when this increase is not offset by workplace recovery, neighborhood shopping and dining weaken, pushing RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days despite RESIDENTIAL staying above its current level and WORKPLACES failing to recover materially.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT improves enough to reduce the commute barrier below about -20 percent from baseline, in-person discretionary trips should broaden and RETAIL_REC should increase within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above -20 and stays there for at least 2 weekly means
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT is currently -26.1 and has improved steadily over four weeks
failure_condition: After TRANSIT crosses above -20 for two weeks, RETAIL_REC fails to improve within the following 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained drop in GROCERY_PHARM after a prior spike signals substitution back toward discretionary shopping trips; that reallocation should push RETAIL_REC upward over the next one to two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls by at least 3 points week-on-week after a 2-week rise
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise within 7 to 14 days after GROCERY_PHARM records a weekly decline of at least 3 points following a short rise.

mechanism_narrative: Strong PARKS mobility together with improving TRANSIT reflects favorable outing conditions that can spill into shopping trips; if both remain elevated, RETAIL_REC should rise over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains flat or declines over the next 28 days despite PARKS staying above 50 and TRANSIT continuing to recover.

mechanism_narrative: In a tightening-restrictions regime, further declines in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT suppress discretionary movement and reduce retail visits, so RETAIL_REC should fall over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both drop by at least 5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days even though both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT each fall by at least 5 points in the same week.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM remains close to its current low level while RESIDENTIAL stays elevated, consumers are consolidating errands near home rather than making discretionary retail trips, which keeps RETAIL_REC below its recent average over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases within 14 days while GROCERY_PHARM stays near current levels and RESIDENTIAL does not fall.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent recovery in WORKPLACES is a lagging indicator of broader in-person activity; once it clears its current depressed range, retail mobility should keep improving over the following month.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises above -25 and stays there for 2 consecutive weekly means
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -42.4 to -25.6 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not exceed its last-4-week mean within 28 days after WORKPLACES moves above -25 for two weeks.
